prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: a square editorial cover illustration for a remote service connection in Factory's MCP library.
Input image 1 is a style reference only. Keep its reductive woodcut and cut-paper character, subtle ink-on-paper texture, bold silhouettes and considered negative space. Do not copy its branching-path composition.
Primary request: depict a compact patch panel with three solid sockets in a vertical column and three broad curved patch cables visibly plugged into them. The panel sits just right of center; cables enter from the left at different heights and converge onto their matching sockets. Treat the cables and their physical plugs as large graphic cut-paper shapes, not thin circuit-board lines. A deliberately rhythmic composition that reads clearly at thumbnail size.
Color palette: deep river-blue ground, warm chalk cables, straw ochre connector sleeves and restrained pale blue-green panel. Full-bleed ink print with irregular carved edges, no surrounding frame. Same small-press cover family as the reference.
Canvas: square, edge-to-edge artwork. Keep the socket column within the central three quarters of the width so a portrait crop retains it.
Constraints: no words, letters, labels, logos, symbols, checks, status lights, UI, screens, books, people, arrows, fake code, gradients or drop shadows. This is an illustration of connectivity, not a factual account status.
